correctness.rationale: The final rank/retract claim follows from a complete explicit normal form. Order, identity and involution force a nondecreasing positive image sequence; implication forbids repeated positive values. Conversely, strictly increasing nonzero tails preserve fusion and implication. Each r-subset gives one rank-(2r+1) map and precisely terminal subsets fix their images. An independently written exhaustive checker tested 11,080 candidate maps for all m,n<=4 and idempotent/rank predictions through m=10; finite tests corroborate but do not replace the general proof.
residual_risks: The pointwise converse depends on the specified standard chain operations; it does not generalize automatically to arbitrary finite Sugihara monoids.

value.rationale: For canonical finite odd Sugihara chains, the complete endomorphism image-rank polynomial, one-to-one correspondence between symmetric image subalgebras and endomorphisms, and exact classification of retracts distinguish natural algebraic invariants. These are motivated full classifications across all chain sizes, not an arbitrary finite slice or mere recomputation of total hom-set sizes.
residual_risks: The classification is elementary and has limited domain; its value does not imply an overarching structural theorem for all Sugihara monoids.

final_claim: REPAIRED final claim: for standard finite odd Sugihara chains S_{2m+1}, endomorphisms are parametrized by subsets of m positive indices, the image-rank polynomial is z(1+z^2)^m, every symmetric subalgebra is the image of one endomorphism, and exactly m+1 idempotents have terminal symmetric interval images, the complete retract list. General hom-set cardinality is previously covered and is credited only as context.
limitations: The hom-set count for arbitrary finite odd Sugihara monoids is already addressed by Aguzzoli–Mordonini (2025, Theorem 5 and Proposition 2); the original novelty framing is superseded and must not be published unchanged.
The revised rank/retract theorem is established only for standard finite odd Sugihara chains, m>=1, not arbitrary finite odd Sugihara monoids.
Its short proof may already be implicit in finite forest duality or an unindexed endomorphism study, notwithstanding the inspected primary sources and index searches.
The independent finite checks cover m,n<=4 and selfmap m<=10 only; arbitrary m follows from the explicit proof.
